title: Route Surface & Road Type Finder
description: Analyse a route's surfaces and road types from OpenStreetMap with the Route Surface & Road Type Finder — paved, gravel, tracks, climb. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a 'mostly paved' tour can turn out to carry 11 miles of gravel and a farm track the road bike would rather know about tonight than meet tomorrow.
quick_answer: The Route Surface & Road Type Finder routes your journey, samples its roads in OpenStreetMap, and reports the recorded surfaces and road types — paved, unpaved, gravel, tracks and more — together with the route's elevation gain. Add start and destination and read what the road is made of.
steps_intro: A route is not one road; it is a census of them. Take the census before the tyres vote:

body.t: Gravel riders hunt unpaved miles; road riders avoid them. Both need the same census — this page takes it. Climb joins from the
A loaded tourer's enemy is the surprise surface at mile 60. Surfaces sampled in advance turn the route into a known quantity.
Low cars, hire cars with unpaved restrictions, classic cars: the surface report is a suitability opinion based on data, not hope.
Two routes, similar distances: the one whose surfaces suit your wheels wins, with the counts as the evidence.
A route advertised by a friend as 'all tarmac' samples at 82% paved, 11% gravel, 7% track. Both riders reroute one section and keep the friendship.
Where OpenStreetMap records no surface, the report says so instead of guessing — an 'unknown' share is part of the census, and on remote routes it can be the biggest slice.

faq: What if a road has no surface recorded?
It is counted as unknown and reported as such. The finder never upgrades a gap into a guess — the unknown share is printed with the rest.
How is the sampling done?
The routed path is sampled along its length and each sample's road is looked up in OpenStreetMap for its surface and type tags; the shares are tallied from the samples.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. Surfaces change with seasons and works, not with traffic.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
The route sampled is the road route — surfaces belong to roads, not to crow lines.
Can route results change over time?
Yes, happily: OpenStreetMap's surface coverage improves as mappers record more roads. A re-run next season can shrink the unknown share.
Does it show elevation too?
Yes — the route's elevation gain rides along, because surface and climb together grade a route's difficulty.
Can it force a gravel-only or paved-only route?
It analyses the route it is given rather than constraining it. Choose or adjust the route with the surface census in hand.
Can it tell me a road is closed?
No — surfaces and types, not closures. A mapped gravel road may still be gated; local signs outrank data.
Why does my route show 100% unknown?
Rural and newly mapped areas can lack surface tags entirely. The census reports the gap; OpenStreetMap improves as mappers pass.
Cobblestone counts as paved?
It is sealed but slow — the report lists it as its own recorded value so you can judge it as your wheels would.
